root_problem: Internal web user access rules are not product-owned because redirect, failure, session, and logout behavior live in implementation guesses, causing security review delay, test rework, and inconsistent homepage access expectations.

user_profile.scenario: opens the internal web system, signs in, checks the homepage identity signal, and signs out before leaving the device
user_profile.current_workaround: treats access behavior as an implementation detail and relies on developers to infer redirect, error, session, and logout rules
user_profile.workaround_cost: downstream design, tests, and implementation can disagree on who may see the homepage and what happens after logout

business_goals: Within the 7-day Phase 1 pilot window, reduce open blocker findings for anonymous homepage access, invalid login, valid login, and logout from any detected blocker to zero before PM delivery.
In the same 7-day observation window, prove 100% of declared web access paths have AC and Verification Plan evidence targets before handoff.
Keep unsupported account lifecycle paths at zero release claims for this phase.

appetite.complexity_ceiling: prove the access loop with one configured account and one homepage surface
appetite.trim_first: registration, password reset, persistent identity administration, role menus, third-party login, visual polish, and production deployment

scope_boundaries: in scope: anonymous homepage redirect to login
in scope: username and password login form
in scope: valid configured credential creates authenticated browser state
in scope: homepage shows current signed-in user and logout entry
in scope: logout clears authenticated state and prevents old-session homepage access
non_goals: do not add user registration or password reset
do not design multi-role authorization or menu permissions
do not build persistent account management
do not specify database schema, API parameters, cookie implementation, framework, or selector details

feasibility_constraints.constraint: one configured account is enough to prove the first access loop
feasibility_constraints.impact_scope: Phase 1 identity behavior and verification evidence
feasibility_constraints.handling: keep PM artifacts at WHAT-layer access behavior and require downstream proof for session, bypass, and logout invalidation

risks_and_unknowns.item: authenticated homepage content may be exposed through direct URL access or stale browser state
risks_and_unknowns.impact: Phase 1 baseline fails if users can see homepage content after logout or without signing in.
risks_and_unknowns.mitigation: PM maps anonymous redirect, logout invalidation, and bypass access rejection to AC and Verification Plan

risks_and_unknowns.item: invalid credential messaging may leak sensitive account state
risks_and_unknowns.impact: Phase 1 scope fails if login failure copy leaks account state while the phase only commits to one configured-account access loop.
risks_and_unknowns.mitigation: PM requires a generic readable error and no authenticated state on failure

decision_rationale.decision: ship one login-to-homepage access loop before broader account capability
decision_rationale.choice: validate anonymous redirect, login success, login failure, homepage identity signal, logout, and old-session rejection in one phase
decision_rationale.rationale: these behaviors form the minimum business-safe entry loop for later homepage work
decision_rationale.excluded_options: registration, account lifecycle, role-based authorization, and production security design are downstream or later-phase work

delivery_plan.goal: deliver the first business-safe login and authenticated homepage loop
